title: ASP.NET Core Identity Setup
description: Set up ASP.NET Core Identity for full user management, including registration, login, password hashing, email confirmation, and role support backed by Entity Framework Core.

blocks.text: What Is ASP.NET Core Identity?

ASP.NET Core Identity is a complete membership system that handles user accounts, password management, role assignments, claims, and authentication tokens. It eliminates the need to build user management from scratch, providing proven implementations for registration, login, password reset, email confirmation, and two-factor authentication.

Identity stores user data in a database using Entity Framework Core. The default schema includes tables for users, roles, user claims, user logins, user tokens, and role claims. When you add Identity to your project, EF Core creates this schema automatically through migrations.

blocks.title: Identity vs. custom authentication
blocks.text: If you only need simple authentication without user management features, cookie or JWT authentication may be simpler. Identity is the right choice when you need registration flows, password reset, role management, or email confirmation out of the box.
Setting Up Identity

To add Identity to an ASP.NET Core project, you install the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore package and register Identity in Program.cs. You also need a DbContext that inherits from IdentityDbContext instead of the standard DbContext.

blocks.title: Installing Identity packages
blocks.content: Add the Identity NuGet package to your project.
blocks.code:
dotnet add package Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore
dotnet add package Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.UI

blocks.text: The Identity.UI package provides pre-built Razor Pages for registration, login, password reset, and other common identity operations. You can scaffold these pages to customize their appearance, or build your own from scratch using the SignInManager and UserManager services.
Configuring the Identity DbContext

The Identity DbContext extends the standard DbContext with Identity-specific DbSet properties for users, roles, and claims. You must inherit from IdentityDbContext<TUser> where TUser is your custom user class.

blocks.title: Custom Identity DbContext
blocks.content: A DbContext configured for Identity with a custom ApplicationUser class.

blocks.text: ApplicationUser extends IdentityUser, which provides standard properties like UserName, Email, PasswordHash, PhoneNumber, and EmailConfirmed. Adding FullName and CreatedAt lets you store additional user profile data without replacing the entire identity schema.
Registering Identity in Program.cs

After creating the DbContext, you register Identity services and configure the default settings. The AddIdentity method wires up UserManager, SignInManager, RoleManager, and all the supporting services.

blocks.title: Identity registration in Program.cs
blocks.content: Full Identity setup with EF Core and default UI.

blocks.text: The AddIdentity call configures password requirements, email confirmation requirements, and account lockout policies. AddEntityFrameworkStores tells Identity to use AppDbContext for storing user data. AddDefaultTokenProviders enables email confirmation and password reset tokens.

blocks.title: Tip: Password policy flexibility
blocks.text: Adjust the password options based on your application's security requirements. For internal tools, you might relax the requirements. For consumer-facing applications, the stricter defaults provide better protection against brute-force attacks.
Using Identity Services

Once Identity is configured, you use two primary services: UserManager<TUser> for user management operations (create, find, update, delete), and SignInManager<TUser> for authentication operations (sign in, sign out, password verification, two-factor authentication).

blocks.title: Registering a new user
blocks.content: Using UserManager to create a user account with a password.

blocks.text: The UserManager.CreateAsync method creates the user and hashes the password before storing it. Passwords are never stored in plain text. The SignInManager then signs the user in by issuing an authentication cookie. The email confirmation token can be sent to the user's email for verification.
Database Migrations for Identity
After configuring Identity, you need to create and apply a migration to generate the identity tables. The identity schema includes tables for users, roles, claims, logins, tokens, and role claims.

blocks.title: Creating and applying the Identity migration
blocks.content: Generate and apply the migration that creates the Identity schema.
blocks.code:
dotnet ef migrations add AddIdentitySchema
dotnet ef database update

blocks.text: After running these commands, your database will have the AspNetUsers, AspNetRoles, AspNetUserClaims, AspNetUserLogins, AspNetUserTokens, AspNetRoleClaims, and AspNetUserRoles tables. These tables are managed by Identity and should not be modified directly.

terms.definition: The base class for Identity user entities, providing standard properties like UserName, Email, and PasswordHash.
The Identity service for managing users — creating, finding, updating, deleting, and validating passwords.
The Identity service for authentication — signing users in, signing out, and handling two-factor authentication.
A DbContext pre-configured with DbSet properties for Identity tables like users, roles, and claims.
Enables token generation for email confirmation, password reset, and two-factor authentication in Identity.

blocks.title: Set Up Identity with Registration and Login
blocks.description: Add ASP.NET Core Identity to a new project, configure it with EF Core, and implement registration and login pages.
steps: Create a new MVC project: 'dotnet new mvc -n IdentityDemo'
Create an ApplicationUser class extending IdentityUser with FullName and CreatedAt properties
Create an AppDbContext inheriting from IdentityDbContext<ApplicationUser>
Configure the connection string in appsettings.json for a local database
In Program.cs, register Identity with AddIdentity, configure password and lockout options, and add AddEntityFrameworkStores and AddDefaultTokenProviders
Add authentication and authorization middleware in the correct order
Create a simple Register and Login controller or use the built-in Identity UI, then run 'dotnet ef migrations add InitIdentity' and 'dotnet ef database update'
Run the app, register a new user, and verify the AspNetUsers table contains the hashed password
blocks.expectedOutcome: Identity is fully configured. A new user can register through the UI, the password is hashed and stored in AspNetUsers, and the user can log in to access protected pages.

blocks.title: ASP.NET Core Identity Summary
points: Identity provides a complete membership system with user management, roles, and claims
ApplicationUser extends IdentityUser to add custom profile properties
IdentityDbContext provides DbSet properties for all Identity tables
UserManager handles user CRUD operations and password validation
SignInManager handles sign-in, sign-out, and two-factor authentication
Migrations create the Identity schema including AspNetUsers, AspNetRoles, and related tables
blocks.takeaway: ASP.NET Core Identity is the standard way to add user management to .NET applications. It handles the complex and security-critical details of password hashing, token generation, and session management so you can focus on your application's features.
